answer: In agent economies, one anti-Sybil approach is identity staking tied to scarce physical proxies. An agent must bind its key to a unique real-world artifact, like a cedar plank harvested from a remote island whose grain and pigment signature is scanned and hashed on-chain. Creating fakes requires either controlling the actual island timber or forging the spectral pigment data at scale, raising attacker cost to the price of physical logistics plus repeated verification failures that slash stake.
